clue.text: B…. difficult woman who has a target to aim at?

definitions.text: who has a target to aim at?

parts.note: the clipped word shown as B with dots stands for the single letter B

indicators.note: difficult here means awkward or contrary, so the letters are made to behave differently and rearrange

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone mutters an expletive about a troublesome woman who seems to have it in for somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'B….' looks like a censored oath but just supplies B; with WOMAN, 'difficult' rearranges the six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An archer shoots arrows at a target, so describing one as someone with a target to aim at fits.

clue.text: Game's HQ having a social event

parts.note: a headquarters is a base of operations
a ball is a formal dance, a social event

explanation.surface: A sports body's headquarters is throwing a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Baseball is a bat-and-ball sport, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Having bagged minimal amount, who'd run badly organised collection?

indicators.note: to bag something is to catch it and hold it, so one piece holds the other inside
a badly organised group is jumbled, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
1p, a single penny, is the smallest sum of British money, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone asks who would run a collection that was messy and raised hardly any money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minimal amount' is 1p, one penny, read as IP; it sits inside the letters of WHO'D RUN, which 'badly organised' reorders.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip-round is an informal collection of money, for instance among colleagues for a leaving present.

clue.text: Demonstrate during international match

parts.note: at can mean during, as in 'at night'
a Test is an international cricket or rugby match

explanation.surface: Fans stage a demonstration in the middle of an international game.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or prove, a synonym of demonstrate in the sense of showing to be true.

clue.text: Son worked hard before exam and buzzed off

parts.note: to cram is to study intensively just before a test

explanation.surface: A boy revised furiously for a test and then took off.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is slang for leave quickly, so having scrammed means having buzzed off.

clue.text: As a man of style, I'd train choirs to present new image

indicators.note: giving the letters a new image means rearranging them into a different form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A choirmaster boasts that training choirs will give them a fresh, stylish image.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian Dior was the French couturier behind the 1947 New Look, a famous man of fashion and style.

clue.text: Slander — talk ultimately coming from nasty speakers

indicators.note: nasty speakers are ugly ones, so the letters of speakers are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word talk

explanation.surface: Slander, in the end, is talk coming from nasty people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming from' says the K at the end of 'talk' is taken out of SPEAKERS; the rest is rearranged by 'nasty'.
explanation.definitionFit: To asperse is to cast aspersions, attacking someone's reputation, which is what slander does.

clue.text: State what's belonging to me, article secured

indicators.note: secured means held fast, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: what belongs to me is mine
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone declares what is theirs, with one item locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is a US state in New England.

clue.text: Becoming old-fashioned like regular sweethearts?

definitions.meaning: something that is ageing visibly is going out of date
couples who go out together regularly are seeing each other romantically

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is going out of date; the other is going out on dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated style is old-fashioned, and couples who go out regularly are said to be courting.

clue.text: Say nothing — one paper is making change

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
I is the Roman numeral one
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone keeps quiet while a newspaper is making changes.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a change of position or direction, synonymous with change.

clue.text: Something painful — thus salesperson has soothing preparation (50% off)

parts.note: so can mean thus, in this way
a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: half the word is taken away, leaving only its first four letters

parts.note: an ointment is a balm or salve

explanation.surface: A salesman with a half-used tub of cream for something that hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: A sore point is a subject that causes hurt or annoyance when raised, so something painful.

clue.text: Nastiest MP has abandoned quality expected of senior politician

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild or unrestrained, so these letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The most unpleasant member of parliament lacks the qualities a senior politician should have.
explanation.definitionFit: Statesmanship is the wisdom and skill in public affairs one hopes for in a leading political figure.

clue.text: Gentleman overwhelmed by a bill set about cafe's employee

indicators.note: set about read as turned around means the whole construction is read backwards
overwhelmed means swamped, so one piece is engulfed by the other

parts.note: a tab is a bill, especially at a bar
sir is the title of a knight or the address to a gentleman

explanation.surface: A gentleman is shocked by a bill and attacks the café's staff member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' looks like 'attacked' but turns the whole construction around after the gentleman goes into the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A barista is someone who makes and serves coffee in a café.

clue.text: Move suddenly, operating — this person might, in emergency?

parts.note: to surge is to rush forward suddenly
on means working or operating, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: In a crisis someone might lurch into action and get things working.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the wordplay: a doctor who might, in an emergency, be operating.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital doctor who performs operations is the person who might operate in an emergency.

clue.text: Vulgar Conservative leaves a pall of gloom?

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so a letter departs from the longer word

parts.note: a cloud is a pall of gloom, as in 'under a cloud'

explanation.surface: A tasteless Tory walks out, leaving a gloomy atmosphere behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud clothes or manners are showy and garish, a sense close to vulgar.

clue.text: Remorseful writer, I will need wine

parts.note: a pen is something you write with
tent is a dark red Spanish wine used as communion wine

explanation.surface: A sorry author says they will need a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is an old name for a deep red Spanish wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Being penitent means feeling sorry for wrongdoing, which is what remorseful means.

clue.text: Finish second half of season in team that's hammered

indicators.note: keeping only the second half of a word means discarding its first three letters

parts.note: winter is one of the four seasons

indicators.note: hammered means battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A team that has been thrashed reaches the end of the second half of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second half of season' is the last half of WINTER, TER; the letters of IN TEAM rearranged by 'that's hammered' give MINATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate something is to end or conclude it, so terminate means finish.

clue.text: Blockage in passage or street accompanied by weird noises

indicators.note: weird means strange, so the letters come out in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An obstruction in an alleyway or road, together with odd sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Stenosis is the medical term for the abnormal narrowing of a body passage such as an artery.

clue.text: Paper dunce Tom makes a hash of

indicators.note: making a hash of something is making a mess of it, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hopeless boy called Tom bungles his written work.
explanation.definitionFit: A document is a written or printed paper, such as an official record.

clue.text: Talk on phone — someone has this legally

parts.note: to chat is to talk informally
tel is the abbreviation for telephone

explanation.surface: Chatting on the phone, someone claims a legal right to something.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, a chattel is an item of movable personal property that someone owns.

clue.text: Black animal, one of a pack?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a rat is an animal

explanation.surface: A dark creature, perhaps a pack animal like a wolf.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brat Pack was a group of young 1980s Hollywood actors, so the 'pack' is not a pack of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Brat Pack, a set of young film stars, were each a brat, one of that pack.

clue.text: Turn down conceited youngster, idiot needing introduction

indicators.note: the idiot must be introduced, that is inserted, into the youngster

parts.note: a pup is a cheeky, conceited young man
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone rejects a cocky young fool who needs to be presented properly.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass up an opportunity is to decline it, to turn it down.

clue.text: Has troubled little man trembled?

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written
Ken is a man's name, short for Kenneth

explanation.surface: Has the short man been so worried that he shook?
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shaken has been made to tremble, so the word fits trembled as a past participle, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Fail to make a mark, maybe a black mark

parts.note: a stain is a mark

explanation.surface: Failing to leave a mark, perhaps a black one, on something.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'mark' in the definition is a voting cross, not a blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from voting, not putting a cross on the ballot paper.

clue.text: Signal of anger keeping opposites apart

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the opposites hold the anger between them
apart says the two letters are separated by the material placed between

parts.note: S and N, south and north, are opposite compass points
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A sign of rage that keeps two opposing sides separated.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a loud warning device, an alarm signal on police cars and ambulances.

clue.text: Nasty hedonistic sot sadly ignored commitment to serve

indicators.note: nasty means unpleasant, so the letters of hedonistic are rearranged
ignored says the letters of sot are left out of the mix

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sad old drunk who loves pleasure neglected his duty.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is German for 'I serve', the motto of the Prince of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The German motto meaning 'I serve' expresses a pledge of service, carried on the Prince of Wales's badge.

clue.text: Rake maybe is casual when meeting royalty

parts.note: a scratch side is put together casually, at short notice
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A dissolute man is casual when he meets the royals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake' looks like a libertine but is a garden tool, an example of something that scratches.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake scrapes the ground, so it is one example of a tool that scratches.

clue.text: Bad brothers having passion to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard signals that the word is spoken, its sound giving the entry

parts.note: a craze is a passion or fad

explanation.surface: Wicked siblings whose passion is to be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Krays were Ronnie and Reggie, twin gangsters in 1960s London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kray twins were notorious East End criminals, so certainly bad brothers.

clue.text: Girl in prison wanting to escape for romance

parts.note: pen is US slang for a penitentiary
to elope is to run off to marry secretly

explanation.surface: A young woman behind bars wants to run off with her lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Penelope is a girl's name.

clue.text: Drives up the wall in French town

definitions.meaning: to drive someone up the wall is to infuriate them
a town in the Loire valley in western France

explanation.definitionFit: To anger people is to drive them mad, and Angers is a town on the Maine in western France.
